set.approach: Park in the round, sandy pullout on the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper, a few kilometres south of the Kerkeslin campground entrance. Behind the pullout a small open field leads to a narrow trail through poplar forest toward Kerkeslin. After the forest the trail steepens; shortly after leaving the aspens take the fork to the left (short cliffs visible ahead mean you have overshot the turn) and follow that trail up a narrow canyon with a creek. The Lower Wall is the first wall on entering the canyon. Colateral Damage is the first route on your left when you enter, alone on the left-hand wall; the others are on the right-hand wall, a little further up.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page plus the route page for where it starts.

set.approach: Drive Maligne Lake Road to its end at the parking lot with the public boat launch, and cross the lake by canoe or kayak, paddling past Spirit Island. Looking south from the island, the climb is on the nearest of the large walls on the western shore, marked by blue streaks down bright white rock. Land below the big scree slope and go up it along the right edge where it meets the forest, with some third and fourth class moves where two small cliff bands cross it. The target is the big corner and gully at the right side of the wall; a third class scramble up that gully reaches a lumpy scree ledge with a few shrubs, the base of the route, and the belay bolt is a few metres to the left.
set.descent_text: The route is equipped to be rappelled: every anchor has rings, and a long rope is needed. Take care on the third pitch's rappel and knot the ends. The single belay bolt at the base also has a ring, for rappelling the scramble below.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page plus the route page for where it starts; descent stated on the route page or its own crag page.

set.approach: The wall is visible from Highway 16 near the east gate of the park. Park in the paved pullout on the highway, then walk west along the highway a short way to an obvious trail on the left. It crosses marshy ground to the base of the wall, with more routes further left along it. Merlin's Warm-Up starts where the trail meets the wall, behind a tall tree stump, at a left-facing corner.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page plus the route page for where it starts.

set.approach: From Jasper, cross the Athabasca River bridge and leave the car in the pullout immediately beyond it. Follow the trail through the opening in the cliff, bearing left. Several side trails branch off, but the bluffs come into view once you top out on the Morro slabs, and any variation leads to the foot of the wall.
